nodes.title: The Conlon–Lee subdivision conjecture

nodes.summary: A simple graph $G$ contains a copy of a simple graph $F$ if there is an injective map $f$ from the vertices of $F$ to the vertices of $G$ such that $f(u)$ and $f(v)$ are adjacent in $G$ whenever $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $F$; the copy need not be induced.
nodes.title: Containing a copy of a graph

nodes.summary: It is not true that for every finite simple graph $H$ and every natural number $r \ge 1$ such that $H$ is bipartite and $r$-degenerate (every nonempty set of vertices contains a vertex with at most $r$ neighbours in that set), the extremal number $\mathrm{ex}(n; H)$ (the largest number of edges of a simple graph on $n$ vertices containing no copy of $H$) is $O(n^{2 - 1/r})$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Counterexample to the Erdős–Simonovits degeneracy conjecture

nodes.summary: The statement that for every finite simple graph $H$ and every natural number $r \ge 1$, if $H$ is bipartite and $r$-degenerate (every nonempty set of vertices contains a vertex with at most $r$ neighbours in that set), then $\mathrm{ex}(n; H) = O(n^{2 - 1/r})$ as $n \to \infty$, where $\mathrm{ex}(n; H)$ is the largest number of edges of a simple graph on $n$ vertices containing no copy of $H$.
nodes.title: Erdős–Simonovits degeneracy conjecture (Erdős Problem 146)

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a simple graph $F$, the extremal number $\mathrm{ex}(n, F)$ is the maximum number of edges of a simple graph on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ that contains no copy of $F$. It is $0$ when every simple graph on these $n$ vertices contains a copy of $F$.
